title: Introducing: Composite Document Layouts (2026 release wave 2)

chapters.title: How composite layouts work - body, theme, and header-footer
Setting themes and headers - layered defaults
Shipped themes and layouts - what comes with 20.9
Live demo - customer statement with multiple themes and headers
Rollout strategy - feature management and layout status

features.name: Composite layouts for documents
features.description: Split report layouts into reusable components - body layout for structure, themes for branding colors and fonts, and header-footer layouts for document headers and footers. Themes and headers-footers can be applied at runtime across different reports.
features.status_evidence_quote: the product group we aim to ship in version 20 9 and 20 1 and send 20 9 1 um three themes approximately
caveats: no changes to default states for shipped layouts in version 2026
feature can be toggled off via feature management

features.name: Body layout
features.description: Structural report layout without styling - defines the raw structure and data presentation of what the report shows, separate from visual branding.

features.name: Theme application
features.description: Apply themes to body layouts at runtime to add colors, fonts, and visual styling. Multiple themes can be applied to the same body layout to show different branding.
features.status_evidence_quote: we aim to ship in version 20.9 and 20.1 and send 20.9.1 um three themes

features.name: Header-footer layout application
features.description: Apply header-footer layouts to body layouts at runtime. Can be set at global, company, report, or specific layout level. Header-footer layouts are divided into external and internal variants.
features.status_evidence_quote: we aim to ship in version 20.9 and 20.1 and send 20.9.1 um three themes, approximately eight um header footer layouts

features.name: Layered layout defaults
features.description: Set default themes and header-footer layouts at global level for all reports, at company level to override global, at report level to override company, or at specific layout level to override report settings.

features.name: Custom theme and header-footer layouts
features.description: Create custom themes and header-footer layouts through the UI on the managed theme and header and footer layouts page, or from AL code by specifying rendering type word with subtype theme or header footer.

features.name: Managed theme and header-footer layouts page
features.description: UI page where users can create new themes or header-footer layouts by name and description, create blank layouts or upload existing ones.

features.name: Shipped themes
features.description: Four themes ship with version 20.9: calm (green, relaxing), default, playful (colors and pink gradient), and standard theme.
features.status_evidence_quote: we aim to ship in version 20.9 and 20.1 and send 20.9.1 um three themes
caveats: documentation mentions three themes but demo shows four: calm, default, playful, standard

features.name: Feature management for composite layouts
features.description: Enable or disable the new document experience via feature management. Can gradually roll out on different environments and for different layouts.

features.name: Layout status control
features.description: Set layout status to retired or draft to hide layouts from users. Even Microsoft-shipped layouts can have their status changed so they do not appear on request pages.
features.status_evidence_quote: we have the ability for you to set the state status of even the the layouts we ship to to either retired or draft.
